messages.author: 8cf245201b2a52eb
messages.subject: knitr2pdf report download in shiny app
parts:
As my first toying around with shiny, I used the template presented here by Brecht Devleesschauwer to generate a shiny app that calculates sample size and generates a pdf report. It works locally and it works on my server when I work interactively over ssh from R with shiny. But when I ask shiny server to run the app for me I can't convince it to execute the knit2pdf function. Any ideas about this? I get the message 'cannot open the connection' in the browser when I click the 'download report' button.

Thanks,
Thomas

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Re: knitr2pdf report download in shiny app
parts:
just to be sure: have you installed all the required packages? have you loaded them explicitly?

If you load them in your local Rprofile / Rsession, then they won't be on your remote.

I personally experienced a problem with rJava on the server: doesn't work. Do you rely on rJava (perhaps as a dependency).

I haven't tried your code I'm afraid, on the phone now. Good luck.

messages.author: 8cf245201b2a52eb
messages.subject: Re: knitr2pdf report download in shiny app
parts: Thanks! that solved half of the problem. I had not called the library(knitr) at the top of server.r, which resulted in the error: 'could not find function "knit2pdf"'. Fixed that and now I consistently get the more criptic error: 'cannot open the connection'. Now I suppose this is a shiny-server configuration issue. I will have to read more about that config I think.

Hi,

I had the same error message in my initial config, because of permissions problem. Check that your shiny user (or the user that you define on your server configuration) got writing rights in your shiny app directory.

Hope this helps,

Robin

messages.author: 8cf245201b2a52eb
messages.subject: Re: knitr2pdf report download in shiny app
parts: Thank you! you hit the nail on the head. I changed the ownership of the shiny-server directory to the shiny user and all is now smooth. I guess I hadn't thought of that because I was running the server as the root. But in the shiny server config file it has the 'run_as shiny' line so I guess that is why the shiny user needs write access to that directory.
